  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The PR-dependency hold check runs after candidate selection, so a held issue can occupy the selector’s single candidate slot on every tick and starve other blocked issues, PRs, and projects.
  WHY: The held issue remains eligible without an `ai:unblock:v1` verdict marker, while `unblock_scan.py select` chooses at most one candidate per tick.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18575-18577 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The jq pre-filter regex does not handle CRLF line endings in issue bodies, so it can miss a PR dependency declaration and skip the dependency hold check.
  WHY: In a CRLF body, the `\r` between `\n` and the declaration prevents the jq regex from matching, so the Python helper that normalizes CRLF is never invoked.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:around line 19060 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The standalone poller's ready-then-post path can write a stale or duplicate `/reclarify` release comment without rechecking readiness or confirming comment history is complete.
  WHY: The ready verdict and comment POST are separate operations, and `history_incomplete` is checked for `verify_history` but not for this path.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: run_unblock_scan, the new `_scan_pr_dependency_status` check inside `while IFS=$'\t' read -r item kind` (about lines 18567-18597). It runs after `python3 scripts/unblock_scan.py select`, around lines 18524 and 18551. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hold check runs after the candidate has already been chosen. `unblock_scan.py` has `effective_limit = 0 if active_judge else min(limit, 1)` and `chosen = candidates[:effective_limit]` (lines 248-249), and its docstring says "Oldest block first, at most one dispatch per tick". When the chosen item is a PR-dependency-held issue, the new code does `continue` and dispatches nothing. A skipped item gets no `ai:unblock:v1` verdict marker, so it is still the oldest candidate on the next tick.
  WHY: Clarify's removal of `ai:blocked` is best-effort and only runs when clarify fires. It only warns on failure, and does not run at all for an issue that was already blocked before this change. A held issue that keeps `ai:blocked` is therefore selected on every tick and skipped on every tick. Because only one candidate is ever chosen, every other blocked issue, PR and project is starved of unblock judging. The skip prevents the held issue's own rounds, but it blocks the whole scan for everyone else. The hold has to be applied before `select`, for example by dropping held issue numbers from `search.json` and `details.json`. Alternatively, dispatch could fall through to the next candidate, which `select` does not support with a limit of 1.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "While held, do not dispatch planning or implementation, request another answer, or consume unblock rounds", delivered as a "tested, fail-closed hold".
  Expected change site: A runtime regression test for `run_unblock_scan`, in `tests/test_unblock_scan.py` or `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`.
  Evidence of absence: The only coverage of the new unblock-scan skip is `test_gates_are_wired_with_trusted_isolated_copies` in `tests/test_pr_dependency.py`. It asserts string ordering in the script source (`scan.index("reason=pr_dependency_held") < scan.index("gh workflow run unblock_judge_dispatch.yml")`) and that the helper call is present. Nothing runs `run_unblock_scan` with a held issue. A source-text test of this kind could not have caught the starvation problem above.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

  PROBLEM: The preflight check for PR dependency declarations using jq may fail to identify declarations in issue bodies containing CRLF line endings.
  WHY: If the issue body uses CRLF, the jq `test` regex `(^|\n)` may not match the carriage return correctly, causing the preflight check to return false. This skips the dependency hold check for an issue that actually has a dependency, leading to unauthorized implementation dispatches.
- scripts/pr_dependency.py:247-248 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The evaluate function catches generic exceptions (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) and returns a held verdict.
  WHY: A transient failure (e.g., gh API returning malformed JSON due to network issues) is treated as a permanent hold condition. This causes unnecessary pipeline blocks instead of allowing the orchestrator to retry the tick when the dependency check might succeed.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: run_unblock_scan (around lines 18567–18596 in the diff context); the while IFS=$'\t' read -r item kind; do loop with the new _scan_pr_dependency_status guard, and scripts/unblock_scan.py:248 (`effective_limit = 0 if active_judge else min(limit, 1)`) plus scripts/unblock_scan.py:249 (`chosen = candidates[:effective_limit]`). | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new hold check sits inside the per-item `while` loop, but `scripts/unblock_scan.py select` caps `effective_limit` at 1 (`min(limit, 1)`) and emits at most one `dispatch` row per tick (line 257 `return {"dispatch": [{"item": number, "kind": kind} for _, number, kind in chosen], ...}`). When the sole candidate is a held issue, the loop body reaches `echo "UNBLOCK_SCAN item=${item} kind=${kind} outcome=skip reason=pr_dependency_held"` and `continue`s, so no `gh workflow run unblock_judge_dispatch.yml` call fires that tick.
  WHY: A held issue consumes the one candidate slot every tick. Because the hold never produces an `ai:unblock:v1` verdict marker, `select` keeps choosing the same held issue on every subsequent tick (it is still blocked, still past `min_blocked`, and still has no recent verdict). Every other blocked issue, PR and failed project sits idle behind it; the unblock scan can never advance past the hold. This contradicts the linked issue's "while held, do not ... consume unblock rounds" intent, which is meant to skip held items without monopolising the scan. `run_standalone_stall_recovery` does not have the same bug because it processes the full `_candidate_details_json` array, not a single-item selection.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: the standalone poller's `test`/`any(...)` predicate around line 19060 and the matching `pr_dependency.py` `evaluate` flow (pr_dependency.py:228–243). | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new flow writes a `/reclarify\n<!-- ai:pr-dependency-released:<n> -->` comment via `gh api .../comments` without first re-checking that the helper still returns `ready` after the second `pulls/<N>` and `contents/<path>` reads race against the default branch. The two-step decision (check ready, then post) is not atomic: the helper call returns the verdict, the code branches to the comment POST, and only then re-emits `STALL_SKIP ... action=reclarify`. Between those moments a force-push that removes `_AI_ENGINE_EXIT_REFUSED` would let a stale `ready` verdict produce a release comment that the next tick will re-evaluate and (correctly) re-hold, but the spurious `/reclarify` is already in the comment history. More importantly, the `comment_count > comments.nodes.length` `history_incomplete` flag is only checked for the `verify_history` path, not for this ready-then-post path; if comments.json is a partial read for any reason, the `if ! any(...)` check returns true and a second release is posted.
  WHY: With a partial comments read, a second release comment is posted, then on the next tick `select` sees a recent verdict marker and skips — but a held issue that genuinely becomes ready between two quick ticks while a comment write is failing can also produce duplicate release comments. The existing security dependency hold has the same one-shot pattern, but it post-conditions the verdict inside the same gh call sequence; this path does not.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Add a tested, fail-closed hold for standalone non-security issues depending on PR #6667. While held, do not dispatch planning or implementation, request another answer, or consume unblock rounds." (from the linked issue body, second sentence.)
  Expected change site: A runtime regression test that exercises `run_unblock_scan` with a held PR-dependency issue and ass
